classification: Informed bounded implementation study; not an independent first-authoring evaluation.
status: Frozen before any compilation/check/run of these first sources; unexecuted.
scope: Existing consume/return operations and apply_contract only. No clean/dirty grammar, new stdlib API, accepted handle, or quantitative-resource claim.
history: Never rewrite attempt-01 after a failure. Keep actual diagnostics separately; any repair needs a later attempt. These expectations are predictions, not observations.

independent_expectations.wire_order: The contract interface is Q<(Bit,Bit)> ordered (D,R), with label d+2*r. Observation order is (E,D,R).
independent_expectations.positive_equation: CNOT(R->D); X(R); CNOT(R->D); X(D) = I_D tensor X_R exactly, with coefficient +1. (d,r)->(d xor r,r)->(d xor r,r xor 1)->(d xor 1,r xor 1)->(d,r xor 1).
independent_expectations.positive_matrix: For every col in 0..4, M[row,col] = 1 iff row = col xor 2; otherwise 0. This is an all-input operator identity, not a known-input simulation claim.
independent_expectations.negative_matrix: For Z(D); X(R), M_bad[row,col] = (-1)^(col mod 2) iff row = col xor 2; otherwise 0. It differs from the specified matrix in columns 1 and 3.
independent_expectations.reference_equation: Starting (|0_E 0_D>+|1_E 1_D>)/sqrt(2) tensor |0_R>, the positive circuit gives the same Bell state tensor |1_R>. The negative gives (|0_E 0_D>-|1_E 1_D>)/sqrt(2) tensor |1_R>. D has marginal I/2 in both; the reference correlation phase differs.

phase-contract-rejected.check: reject the exact function contract; do not run the rejected contracted program
phase-contract-rejected.diagnostic: expect a contract/equation mismatch; actual code/span/message must be captured, not assumed

phase-reference-observed.check: accept the uncontracted declared observing program
phase-reference-observed.run: after inverse Bell preparation, P[(E,D,R)=(1,0,1)] = 1; acceptance makes no dirty-restoration claim

independent_expectations.bounds: Two-qubit operator contract; at most three physical qubits in the Bell experiment. No maximum-size cases.
independent_expectations.limits: Numerical Bell observations do not prove arbitrary-reference restoration. Fresh exact native contract evidence and existing semantic lemmas have separate scopes.
